## NFL injury briefing

### Big status changes
- **Cardinals WR Jalen Brooks** — will miss the **rest of the season** after revealing he needs **emergency wrist surgery**.
  - **Why it matters:** Arizona loses a depth receiver/possible rotational target for the stretch run.
  - **Watch next:** recovery timeline after surgery; no return this season.

- **Panthers RT Taylor Moton** — will undergo **season-ending ankle surgery** while also dealing with a **fractured fibula in his left leg**.
  - **Why it matters:** Carolina takes a major hit on the offensive line and pass protection.
  - **Watch next:** how the Panthers shuffle the right tackle spot.

- **Seahawks LT Charles Cross** — has a **high ankle sprain** and is **expected to miss time**.
  - **Why it matters:** Seattle is losing a key blindside protector, which can affect QB comfort, play-calling, and fantasy ceiling for the offense.
  - **Watch next:** whether he lands on a short-term absence or misses multiple games.

- **Packers injury update** — **Sean Rhyan** and **Zaire Franklin** are **likely to miss time**, per the report, though the excerpt cuts off before more detail.
  - **Why it matters:** Green Bay’s depth is being tested after the Week 7 loss to Detroit.
  - **Watch next:** specifics on the injuries and whether either player is ruled out for Week 8.

That keeps the outside-receiver rotation open, but the staff’s comments still point more toward Williams absorbing the target bump than Burks taking over the whole role this week. [2, 3, 4]

That suggests a slightly cleaner game plan is the main path to a better passing environment, but the concrete fantasy change is still the Williams/Diggs redistribution above. [1, 7, 8]

BAL.summary:
- **Lamar Jackson (QB)** — Jesse Minter said Jackson could be available Sunday, which makes him the single biggest swing factor in Baltimore’s Week 8 projections. If he returns after three weeks out, Tyler Huntley goes back to a backup role and the Ravens’ skill players get a major efficiency boost; if Jackson isn’t cleared, the offense stays in a lower-ceiling Huntley setup. [9, 3, 10]

- **Derrick Henry (RB)** — Week 7 showed a real committee, with Henry and Justice Hill splitting snaps almost evenly (34 to 31) while the run game stayed inefficient. That keeps Henry from projecting as a pure workhorse this week and preserves enough Hill usage to matter in PPR/DFS lineups. [1]

- **Zay Flowers (WR)** — Flowers remains Baltimore’s clear passing-game alpha; he entered Week 8 leading all receivers in yards per route run and ranked No. 1 in separation score among qualified wideouts. Against a Buffalo secondary missing a starter, he’s the Raven most likely to turn target volume into explosive production, especially if Jackson is active. [2]

- **Rashod Bateman (WR)** — Bateman and Ja’Kobi Lane were nearly even in Week 7 snaps behind Flowers (49 for Bateman, 46 for Lane), with Devontez Walker down at 20. That keeps the WR2/WR3 pecking order muddy enough that Bateman is more volatile than Flowers for this week’s projections. [1]

- **Emery Jones Jr. (OL)** — Jones finished Week 7 at right guard after Vega Ioane’s knee injury, with Cam Jurgens already locked in at center. Given Baltimore’s existing interior-line losses, that line instability still threatens both pocket security and Henry’s rushing efficiency this week. [1]
